modules.title: Benefit-led chapter stack
modules.study: Each chapter pairs a short emotional headline with product imagery and practical proof points.
modules.reuse: Use for premium products where the buyer needs confidence across migration, durability, software, and support.

modules.title: Explore the lineup
modules.study: Moves from narrative to model comparison with colors, claims, learn-more links, and buy links.
modules.reuse: Use when a brand has multiple SKUs and needs choice support without leaving the campaign page.

modules.title: Trade-in and support reassurance
modules.study: Purchase paths are reinforced by trade-in, help, and support messages.
modules.reuse: Pair high-consideration CTAs with reassurance modules that reduce purchase anxiety.

modules.title: Offer-first hero
modules.study: The page foregrounds price and order intent instead of delaying conversion until the end.
modules.reuse: Use for high-consideration products when a known buyer may arrive ready to configure.

modules.title: Trade-in incentive
modules.study: A concrete incentive creates a reason to start the purchase process now.
modules.reuse: Use for categories where replacement timing is a meaningful conversion lever.

modules.title: Spec table as confidence layer
modules.study: Key numbers such as range and acceleration anchor the emotional story in measurable claims.
modules.reuse: Use compact specs near CTA paths to support fast comparison.

modules.title: Claim-plus-basket hero
modules.study: A product claim stack, price, rating, stock status, and add-to-basket CTA live in one commerce block.
modules.reuse: Use for technical products where proof and purchase must be visible together.

modules.title: Attachments and service details
modules.study: Accessories, attachments, support, and app guidance extend confidence beyond the initial purchase.
modules.reuse: Use for hardware products whose value depends on ecosystem and upkeep.

modules.title: Scientific feature evidence
modules.study: Claims such as illumination and dust detection make invisible value tangible.
modules.reuse: Turn technical mechanisms into visible proof modules.

modules.title: Business model solution grid
modules.study: A broad product suite becomes a set of audience-specific entry points.
modules.reuse: Use when a platform serves several business models and cannot rely on a single product CTA.

modules.title: Global metric band
modules.study: Currencies, payment volume, uptime, and subscriptions create enterprise-grade trust.
modules.reuse: Use verified scale metrics as a structural trust band near the top third of the page.

modules.title: Start now and contact sales
modules.study: Self-serve and sales motions are both exposed early.
modules.reuse: Use dual CTAs when the product spans startups, platforms, and enterprises.

modules.title: Campaign slogan hero
modules.study: A punchy headline, product name, benefit line, and shop CTA create fast retail momentum.
modules.reuse: Use for seasonal campaigns where brand energy and purchase path should be immediate.

modules.title: Shop by Category
modules.study: Image-led category tiles split the broad audience into useful shopping paths.
modules.reuse: Use category tiles when a campaign must serve multiple intent levels.

modules.title: Shop by Cushioning Type
modules.study: Product families are organized by user need rather than internal SKU logic.
modules.reuse: Use need-state comparison for consumer products with confusing feature families.

modules.title: Feature-first organization module
modules.study: Pocket internals, lockable zipper, laptop fit, and removable compression pad make the storage system legible before checkout.
modules.reuse: Use for premium travel or utility products whose value depends on internal organization details.

modules.title: Measurement and compatibility block
modules.study: Trip length, weight, volume, dimensions, and airline-fit guidance answer the most practical buyer questions in one place.
modules.reuse: Pair emotional product styling with a dense utilitarian block when buyers need operational confidence.

modules.title: Trial-and-warranty reassurance rail
modules.study: The 100-day trial, lifetime warranty, and optional coverage shift the CTA from risk to confidence.
modules.reuse: Use stacked reassurance when the product is premium-priced and buyers expect longevity protection.

modules.title: Three-benefit wearable hero
modules.study: A tight hero stack links sensing accuracy, discreet comfort, and battery longevity to immediate product desirability.
modules.reuse: Use for compact devices where the buyer needs a fast read on what materially improved.

modules.title: Metrics and membership value section
modules.study: Health domains such as sleep, stress, heart health, and women's health turn the membership pitch into concrete outcome categories.
modules.reuse: Organize subscription value around outcomes, not abstract platform language.

modules.title: Sizing and FAQ reassurance block
modules.study: Sizing-kit guidance, lab-validation language, and environmental durability notes reduce return anxiety for a ring-sized device.
modules.reuse: Use a support block when the physical fit of the product materially affects confidence and performance.

modules.title: Feature-icon premium hero
modules.study: Price, add-to-cart, color choice, and a short icon row communicate the offer quickly without flattening the brand tone.
modules.reuse: Use a concise feature icon rail when a premium product needs scannability without becoming commodity e-commerce.

modules.title: Acoustic and comfort proof stack
modules.study: The page alternates close product detail, lifestyle imagery, and short proof paragraphs to sustain a long premium narrative.
modules.reuse: Break dense product proof into alternating sensory chapters when each benefit needs its own emotional framing.

modules.title: Bundle and set upsell block
modules.study: A personal-entertainment bundle and pair discount create a higher-order purchase path after the product story lands.
modules.reuse: Use bundles once the core product narrative is established, not before the buyer understands the base offer.

modules.pageTitle: The product development system for teams and agents
modules.title: Live product theater hero
modules.study: The opening frame behaves like a miniature product session with issues, reviews, agent actions, and workspace structure visible at once.
modules.reuse: Use a live product canvas when the product's speed and information architecture are core proof, not just supporting visuals.

modules.title: Battery benchmark band
modules.study: Streaming, web usage, conferencing, and standby metrics establish multiple real-world proof modes instead of one synthetic number.
modules.reuse: Use scenario-based benchmarks when technical buyers need to map claims to their own working day.

modules.title: Ports and personalization module

modules.reuse: Show modular parts as a clear kit-of-parts UI when customization is central to the offer.

modules.title: Repair and upgrade ownership block
modules.study: QR-code guides, single-tool repair, and Marketplace upgrades keep maintenance in the main sales narrative instead of support documentation.
modules.reuse: Promote repair and upgrade flows into primary product proof when longevity is part of the value proposition.

modules.title: DIY versus pre-built purchase split
modules.study: Two purchase paths let expert buyers choose operating-system control or out-of-box convenience without fragmenting the page.
modules.reuse: Offer parallel configuration paths when the audience spans enthusiasts and buyers who want a ready-to-run system.

modules.title: Configure-first premium hero
modules.study: Price, configure CTA, included marker, free shipping, and 50-day trial all sit inside a minimal hardware stage.
modules.reuse: Use for premium hardware when the first screen has to feel quiet and luxurious while still letting ready buyers act immediately.

modules.title: Bundle ladder
modules.study: Marker, folio, and keyboard bundles turn accessories into an understandable progression instead of a fragmented accessory shelf.
modules.reuse: Package core accessories as guided bundles when they materially change how the product is used.

modules.title: Feature specification stack
modules.study: Feature prose transitions into detailed hardware and software specifications without losing narrative rhythm.
modules.reuse: Use a narrative-to-spec handoff when the buyer needs both emotional confidence and technical due diligence.

modules.title: Compare and ecosystem handoff
modules.study: Buyer guide, comparison, desktop/mobile apps, and cloud support keep the product inside a broader workflow ecosystem.
modules.reuse: Add comparison and ecosystem links when a premium device purchase depends on workflow fit, not just the object itself.

modules.title: System explainer hero
modules.study: The hero uses one product family explanation to set up cooling, elevation, sound, and whole-bed transformation before narrower persona stories.
modules.reuse: Use when one premium system needs to feel bigger than a single SKU without overwhelming visitors on the first screen.

modules.title: Persona problem grid
modules.study: Persona cards translate one technology stack into distinct use cases with dedicated imagery and concise emotional copy.
modules.reuse: Segment the page by user problem when the same core product solves very different pain points.

modules.title: Clinical results band
modules.study: Large percent metrics and science framing provide a conversion-grade proof layer before the testimonial carousel.
modules.reuse: Surface quantifiable outcomes when premium pricing requires evidence beyond aesthetic storytelling.

modules.title: Testimonial and review stack
modules.study: Named quotes, personas, and long-form review snippets make the page feel validated by real routines, not generic brand copy.
modules.reuse: Use stacked social proof when the buyer needs reassurance that the product changes daily behavior, not just features.

modules.title: Free-start hero with working UI stage
modules.study: The page puts a free CTA beside a dense inbox mockup so the launch feels both approachable and already operational.
modules.reuse: Use when a software launch needs to prove immediate utility on the first screen without looking like a static ad.

modules.title: Scenario-led view rail
modules.study: Candidate hiring, support triage, travel, and newsletter views translate the same core product into distinct job-to-be-done entry points.
modules.reuse: Break one workflow product into labeled scenarios when the buyer needs to picture personal adoption before understanding every feature.

modules.title: Search, views, calendar, and auto-label stack
modules.study: Search, saved views, calendar integration, and auto-labeling are shown together so the product reads like an opinionated workspace, not just a smarter inbox.
modules.reuse: Group automation, organization, and scheduling inside one coherent product frame when the value comes from orchestration rather than a single feature.

modules.title: Social proof feed
modules.study: Short testimonial quotes from recognizable operators make the launch feel contemporary and community-validated instead of enterprise-corporate.
modules.reuse: Use a compact quote wall when a product wins by word-of-mouth credibility and workflow relatability more than by hard procurement proof.

modules.title: Launcher hero with immediate download path
modules.study: The hero pairs a terse value claim with Mac and Windows entry points, keeping the product legible for both curious browsers and ready installers.
modules.reuse: Use a minimal hero when the category is already known and the page needs to communicate polish, speed, and intent before detail.

modules.title: Product-family navigation as proof
modules.study: Store, Pro, AI, Teams, Developers, iOS, and Windows appear as first-class routes, making the ecosystem breadth part of the marketing surface.
modules.reuse: Expose adjacent product surfaces early when your expansion strategy is itself a trust signal.

modules.title: Pro capability stack
modules.study: AI, Cloud Sync, Clipboard History, Window Management, Notes, and custom themes show how the core launcher grows into a personalized desktop system.
modules.reuse: Group premium features as a coherent operating environment when upsell value comes from cumulative workflow depth, not one marquee add-on.

modules.title: Practitioner testimonial wall
modules.study: Quotes and identities from builders, designers, and creators make the page feel like a tool chosen by people with high workflow standards.
modules.reuse: Use a dense expert-social-proof section when the product benefits from taste signaling as much as from raw specs.

modules.title: Editorial hardware hero
modules.study: Large product imagery, short declarative copy, and a dark palette make the page feel like a printed campaign for one object.
modules.reuse: Use when a premium device needs to feel singular and collectible before the visitor reads deeper technical proof.

modules.title: Capability paragraph beside product proof
modules.study: Features are grouped into readable capability bursts instead of a long engineering list, keeping the product page emotional and technical at the same time.
modules.reuse: Pair short capability clusters with close product framing when the audience values craft but still needs concrete proof.

modules.title: Integrated store handoff
modules.study: The product page and store page share language, imagery, and accessories so the transition from inspiration to checkout does not feel like a context switch.
modules.reuse: Keep commerce in the same visual system when brand taste is part of why the product commands a premium price.

modules.title: Category-defining hero with immediate buy and demo paths
modules.study: The overview page introduces the device with dual conversion actions so curious visitors can either learn or commit without leaving the category frame.
modules.reuse: Use paired demo and purchase actions when the product is expensive, unfamiliar, or best understood through guided experience.

modules.title: Hardware anatomy stack
modules.study: Band, Light Seal, speakers, crown, and battery are explained as distinct comfort and control systems rather than one technical blob.
